generation.explanation: This is the classic base rate fallacy, solved with Bayes' theorem. Out of 1,000 people, only about 10 are sick, and 9 of them test positive — but 99 of the 990 healthy people also (falsely) test positive. So of the 108 positive tests, only 9 are actually sick: 9/108 ≈ 8.3%. Even a 90%-accurate test gives a surprising result because the disease is rare; drag the sliders to see how prevalence, sensitivity, and specificity change the answer.
